description: Retrieval priors for recurring natural-language gaps between player questions and official MTG rules. These entries boost official evidence retrieval only; they must not contain final answers.

priors.reason: Player wording often names the counter action while the rules store it under keyword actions.
Questions about uncounterable spells usually need both can't-beats-can and countering rules.
Common player shorthand for spells that can't be countered.
Player questions often ask whether a permission can override a prohibition.
Static abilities are a broad rule category and are often asked using exact terminology.
Questions asking how to identify activated abilities need the activated ability definition.
Questions about whether mana abilities use the stack need both mana ability timing and stack exceptions.
Questions about responding to playing lands need land play timing and special action rules.
Questions about all targets becoming illegal at resolution map to resolving spells and abilities.
Questions about attacking or tap abilities soon after control changes need the creature timing restriction.
Questions about copied spells retaining targets, modes, or other choices need the copy-of-spell rules.
Questions about when spell modes are chosen need the casting spell choices step.
Questions using the split second keyword need its keyword rule.
Questions about when instants can be cast need instant timing and priority rules.

priors.pattern: \b(double strike|deals? combat damage|combat damage)\b.*\b(whenever|trigger(?:s|ed)?|create[sd]?)\b|\b(whenever|trigger(?:s|ed)?|create[sd]?)\b.*\b(double strike|deals? combat damage|combat damage)\b
priors.reason: This combines three official concepts: triggered abilities, double strike, and combat damage steps.
Player wording about being targeted maps to the targeting definition and the rule that affected objects are not automatically targets.

priors.pattern: \b(leaves? the game|loses? the game)\b.*\b(owner|owned|control|permanent|object)\b|\b(owner|owned|control|permanent|object)\b.*\b(leaves? the game|loses? the game)\b
priors.reason: Questions about owned objects after a player loses need losing/leaving-game and multiplayer object handling rules.

priors.pattern: \b(state[- ]based action|state based actions|sba|sbas|dies?|death trigger|trigger(?:s|ed)?|put on the stack|priority)\b.*\b(state[- ]based action|state based actions|sba|sbas|dies?|death trigger|trigger(?:s|ed)?|put on the stack|priority)\b
priors.reason: Timing questions about death triggers and state-based actions need the priority loop, trigger creation, trigger stacking, and SBA timing rules.
